chunks: And from him, from Abu al-Husayn al-Nakha'i, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a person in ihram who had intercourse with his wife. He said: 'Upon him is a she-camel.'
Zurarah said to him: 'I have asked him about what you asked him about, and he said to me:
As for that which indicates that intercourse in the private part is specifically indicated, unlike other acts, is what has been narrated:

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A she-camel, a specific type of animal used as expiation in Islamic law
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurarah ibn A'yan, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (sacred consecration) for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim in ihram who has sexual intercourse with their spouse?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific expiation for a muhrim engaging in sexual intercourse, prescribing a *badanah* (a mature camel or its equivalent in cattle/sheep) and the obligation to return for Hajj the following year. The narration highlights the scholarly distinction made by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) between intercourse in the private part versus other acts, establishing a precise legal boundary for the severity of the penalty. This ruling underscores the seriousness of violating the sanctity of the sacred state during pilgrimage.
